items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Ikoma-san thought I should study with him... I went to his place, where he‟s playing

ctx.x: [Laughs]. Anyway, so I was actually pretty in demand, because I was playing like Teddy Wilson style, everything was that. And there was a number one pianist in those days, his name was Mister Matsui, Hachirō Matsui. He had, he was playing with a small group, and there was another department store, the top floor, and, uh, Ikoma-san thought I should study with him. So he says, “Well, I don‟t teach, but if you want to come watch me play, it‟s fine.” So off-days, which was quite often, I went to his place, where he‟s…
